newsitem.title: CHINA: China supports Taiwan opening to mainland media.
newsitem.headline: China supports Taiwan opening to mainland media.

text.p: China said on Tuesday it supported a decision by rival Taiwan to allow mainland Chinese journalists to report from the island for up to two years.
"We have always favoured strengthening personnel exchanges between the two sides," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a regular news briefing.
"Supporting the realisation of the 'three links' was also proposed by our side," Cui said in reference to proposed trade, travel and mail connections between China and Taiwan.

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council, a cabinet level policy making body, said on Monday it would soon start accepting applications from Chinese reporters to work on the island for up to one year, with the possiblity of extension for another year.
Taiwan has banned direct links with the communist mainland since a civil war separated the two in 1949.
The island allows mainland Chinese journalists to visit on a case-by-case basis.
China permits approved Taiwan journalists to stay in Beijing for about one month.
Beijing has been eager to open direct air and sea links with the thriving island but Taipei has refused, seeing such links as its last bargaining chip in talks on reunification.
China last August issued rules governing direct shipping across the Taiwan Strait in what it hoped would be a framework for such links in future.
